description.p: Wherever they come from, pugilists live a rough and tumble life that leaves them full of determination and reckless grit. In a fight they channel this strength of character to dig deep and fight off foes with greater strength of numbers, arms, or armor than anyone else would think possible.
Pugilists tap into their own inner strength in the form of moxie. This is not mystical energy, but determination forged over a lifetime of hardship and a never-say-die attitude.
Pugilists come from the rougher corners of the world: alleys, fighting rackets, taverns, ghettos, arenas, and any place where fists settle arguments faster than words.
You can make a pugilist quickly by making Strength your highest ability score, followed by Constitution. Second, choose the criminal or urchin background.
As a pugilist, you gain the following class features.

ul.li: Hit Points at 1st Level: 8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per pugilist level after 1st
Weapons: Simple weapons, improvised weapons, whip, hand crossbow. Compatibility note: some proficiencies may need to be added manually depending on Aurora build.
Tools: Your choice of one artisan’s tools, gaming set, or thieves’ tools. Add this manually if your Aurora build does not prompt for it.
Skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Intimidation, Perception, Sleight of Hand, and Stealth

sheet.description: A streetfighter with swagger to spare, powered by moxie and hard-won grit.

setters.set: A streetfighter with swagger to spare, powered by moxie and hard-won grit.

description.p: Pugilists in the Arena Royale fight club travel the world earning their keep as equal parts performer and gladiator.

sheet.description: Arena Royale features: Bonus Proficiency and Persona Libre at 3rd level, Work the Crowd at 6th, High Flyer at 11th, and Signature Move at 17th.

description.p: Bloodhound Bruisers are notorious for looking for trouble and finding it every time, using observation and streetwise instinct to defend the downtrodden or serve less savory ends.

sheet.description: Bloodhound Bruisers features: Ever Vigilant and Detective Work at 3rd level, Scrap Like a Sleuth at 6th, Heart of the City at 11th, and Eyes Wide Open at 17th.

description.p: Pugilists in the Dog & Hound fight club rely on the best four-legged friend a body could ask for.

sheet.description: Dog & Hound features: Bonus Proficiency, Brawler’s Best Friend, and Mutt With Moxie at 3rd level, Arcanine Bite and Coordinated Attack at 6th, Hound’s Best Friend at 11th, and Dire Hound at 17th.

description.p: Pugilists in the Piss & Vinegar fight club revel in their reputations as heels, using curses and dirty tricks to provoke and win.

sheet.description: Piss & Vinegar features: Bonus Proficiency and Salty Salute at 3rd level, Dirty Tricks at 6th, Mean Old Cuss at 11th, and The Uncouth Art at 17th.

description.p: Pugilists who fight in the Squared Circle know you do not have to knock an opponent senseless to get them to submit, though they often do both.

sheet.description: The Squared Circle features: Groundwork at 3rd level, Meat Shield at 6th, Heavyweight at 11th, and Clean Finish at 17th.

description.p: Pugilists who practice the Sweet Science hit hard, fast, and often.

sheet.description: The Sweet Science features: Cross Counter at 3rd level, One, Two, Three, Floor at 6th, Float Like a Butterfly, Sting Like a Bee at 11th, and Knock Out at 17th.

description.p: At 1st level, your years of fighting in back alleys and taverns have given you mastery over combat styles that use unarmed strikes and pugilist weapons, which are simple melee weapons without the two-handed property, whips, and improvised weapons. You may not use the finesse property of a weapon while using it as a pugilist weapon.
You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or using only pugilist weapons and you are wearing light or no armor and not using a shield:

ul.li: You can roll your Fisticuffs die in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or pugilist weapon.
When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike or grapple as a bonus action.

sheet.description: Your Fisticuffs die is 1d{{pugilist:fisticuffs:dice}}. While unarmed or using only pugilist weapons, wearing light or no armor, and not using a shield, you can use this die for your unarmed strike or pugilist weapon damage. When you take the Attack action with an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon, you can make one unarmed strike or grapple as a bonus action.

description.p: Beginning at 1st level, you can use Constitution instead of Dexterity to determine your Armor Class when you are wearing light or no armor and are not using a shield.

sheet.description: While wearing no armor and not using a shield, your AC is {{ac:iron chin pugilist}}. The light armor substitution from Iron Chin should be handled manually.

description.p: Starting at 2nd level, your experience laying the beatdown on others has given you moxie you can channel in battle. Your pugilist level determines the maximum number of moxie points you have, as shown in the Pugilist table.

You can spend these points to fuel various moxie features. You start knowing Brace Up, The Old One-Two, and Stick and Move. You regain all expended moxie points when you complete a short or long rest.

sheet.description: You have {{pugilist:moxie}} moxie points, regained when you complete a short or long rest. You can spend moxie on Brace Up, The Old One-Two, Stick and Move, and other features you gain later.

description.p: You can use a bonus action and spend 1 moxie point to brace for attacks. Roll your Fisticuffs die + your pugilist level + your Constitution modifier and gain that many temporary hit points.

sheet.description: Roll 1d{{pugilist:fisticuffs:dice}}+{{pugilist:brace up bonus}} and gain that many temporary hit points.

description.p: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, you can spend 1 moxie point to make two unarmed strikes as a bonus action.

sheet.description: Immediately after you take the Attack action on your turn, spend 1 moxie point to make two unarmed strikes.

description.p: You can use a bonus action and expend 1 moxie point to make a shove attack or take the Dash action.

sheet.description: Spend 1 moxie point to make a shove attack or take the Dash action.

description.p: Beginning at 2nd level, carousing, shadowboxing, and sparring all count as light activity for the purposes of resting for you. Additionally, once you have caroused in a settlement for 8 hours or more, you know all public locations in the city as if you were born and raised there and you cannot be lost by non-magical means while within the city.

sheet.description: Carousing, shadowboxing, and sparring count as light activity for resting. After carousing in a settlement for 8 hours or more, you know all public locations there and cannot be lost by non-magical means while within the city.

description.p: Starting at 3rd level, when you take damage that reduces you to half your maximum hit points or less, you can use your reaction to gain temporary hit points equal to your pugilist level + your Constitution modifier and regain all expended moxie points. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

sheet.description: When damage reduces you to half your maximum hit points or less, use your reaction to gain {{pugilist:bloodied but unbowed temp hp}} temporary hit points and regain all expended moxie points.

description.p: Starting at 3rd level, you choose a fight club that best exemplifies your style: Arena Royale, Bloodhound Bruisers, Dog & Hound, Piss & Vinegar, the Squared Circle, or the Sweet Science. Your fight club grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

sheet.description: Choose a fight club. It grants features at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

description.p: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or two ability scores by 1. You cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

Starting at 4th level, you discover a strength inside you that can’t be broken. As a bonus action, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage for one minute. At the end of that minute you gain a level of exhaustion.

sheet.description: Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage for 1 minute. At the end of that minute, you gain one level of exhaustion.

description.p: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

sheet.description: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

description.p: Starting at 5th level, before you make an attack roll with an unarmed strike or pugilist melee weapon attack that does not already have disadvantage, you can declare you are swinging wild haymakers. You make all attack rolls until the end of this turn with disadvantage and when you deal damage you do not roll, but use the maximum die result instead.

sheet.description: Before an unarmed strike or pugilist melee weapon attack that does not already have disadvantage, you can declare haymakers. Your attack rolls until the end of this turn have disadvantage, and when you deal damage you use the maximum die result instead of rolling.

description.p: Starting at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks and damage.

sheet.description: Your unarmed strikes count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks and damage.

description.p: At 7th level, you gain proficiency in Dexterity saving throws.

sheet.description: You gain proficiency in Dexterity saving throws.

description.p: Starting at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

sheet.description: End one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

description.p: At 9th level, when you use your Bloodied but Unbowed feature you can choose to also use this feature. If you do, you add your proficiency bonus to your damage with unarmed attacks and pugilist weapons for the next minute. You can use this feature again after you complete a long rest.

sheet.description: When you use Bloodied but Unbowed, you can add your proficiency bonus to damage with unarmed attacks and pugilist weapons for 1 minute.

description.p: By 10th level, you have resistance to psychic damage and gain advantage on saving throws against effects that would make you stunned or unconscious.

sheet.description: You have resistance to psychic damage and advantage on saving throws against effects that would make you stunned or unconscious.

description.p: Starting at 13th level, once you have taken a long rest by carousing in a settlement, you gain advantage on all Charisma (Persuasion) and Charisma (Intimidation) checks made against the people who live there.

sheet.description: After taking a long rest by carousing in a settlement, you gain advantage on Charisma (Persuasion) and Charisma (Intimidation) checks made against the people who live there.

description.p: Starting at 14th level, you gain advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 moxie point to reroll it and take the second result.

sheet.description: You have advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. When you fail a saving throw, you can spend 1 moxie point to reroll it and take the second result.

description.p: At 15th level, your carrying capacity is doubled, and when you deal damage with a melee weapon or unarmed strike to an inanimate object that damage is doubled. Your standing jump distance is the same as your running start jump distance.

sheet.description: Your carrying capacity is doubled. Damage you deal to inanimate objects with melee weapons or unarmed strikes is doubled. Your standing jump distance is the same as your running start jump distance.

description.p: Starting at 18th level, when you have 4 levels of exhaustion or fewer and are reduced to 0 hit points, you regain half your maximum hit points, half your maximum moxie points, and gain a level of exhaustion. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

sheet.description: When you have 4 levels of exhaustion or fewer and are reduced to 0 hp, regain half your maximum hp and half your maximum moxie points, then gain one level of exhaustion.

description.p: At 20th level, your Strength and Constitution ability scores increase by 2 to a maximum of 22. Additionally, when you take a long rest you recover 2 levels of exhaustion instead of 1 and regain all expended hit dice instead of half your expended hit dice.

sheet.description: Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by 2, to a maximum of 22. When you take a long rest, you recover 2 levels of exhaustion instead of 1 and regain all expended hit dice instead of half.

description.p: Starting when you choose this Fight Club at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Performance skill if you do not have it already. If you do, you gain proficiency in your choice of Intimidation or Persuasion.

sheet.description: You gain proficiency in Performance. If you already have it, choose Intimidation or Persuasion instead.

description.p: Also at 3rd level, you create an alternate persona that you can adopt or discard as a bonus action on your turn. Unless you tell a creature, or the creature sees you adopt your persona, they do not know you and the adopted persona are the same person.

You have a pool of persona points equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). While you have adopted your persona, you can spend persona points instead of moxie points, and before you make a Charisma ability check you can spend a persona point to add your Strength modifier to the result. You regain all expended persona points when you finish a long rest.

sheet.description: As a bonus action, adopt or discard your alternate persona. While adopted, you can spend persona points instead of moxie points and can spend a persona point before a Charisma check to add your STR modifier. Persona points: {{pugilist:persona points}}/Long Rest (minimum 1).

description.p: At 6th level, while you have adopted your alternate persona, you can use your action to inspire fear or adoration in those nearby. Creatures within 30 feet who can see you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed, if you chose adoration, or frightened, if you chose fear, for 1 minute. Each time a creature takes damage from you or one of your allies it can repeat the save, ending the effect on a success. You can use this feature again after you finish a long rest.

sheet.description: While your persona is adopted, creatures within 30 ft. who can see you must make a WIS save against DC {{pugilist:arena royale:dc}} or be charmed or frightened for 1 minute. Damaged creatures repeat the save.

description.p: Starting at 11th level, your base movement increases by 10 feet, your jump distance is doubled, and you can use a bonus action on your turn to take the Dash action.

sheet.description: Your base movement increases by 10 feet, your jump distance is doubled, and you can Dash as a bonus action.

description.p: Starting at 17th level, you create a signature move that you can use while you have adopted your alternate persona. You can replace one unarmed attack or pugilist weapon attack on your turn with this signature move. When you do, you can jump in any direction up to your movement speed, make an attack roll with advantage against a creature in your reach and, if you hit, the attack is a critical and the creature is stunned until the end of your next turn. If you hit, you must finish a long rest before you can use it again. If you miss, you regain the use after 1 minute.

sheet.description: While your persona is adopted, replace one unarmed or pugilist weapon attack with your signature move. Jump up to your speed, attack with advantage, and on a hit the attack is critical and stuns until the end of your next turn. Hit: recharge on long rest. Miss: recharge after 1 minute.

description.p: When you choose this fight club at 3rd level, you have advantage on initiative rolls. During the first round of combat, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures who haven’t acted yet.

sheet.description: You have advantage on initiative rolls. During the first round of combat, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures who have not acted yet.

description.p: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Insight, Investigation, or Perception. In addition, when you make an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Insight), or Wisdom (Perception) check, you can spend 1 moxie point to gain advantage on that ability check.

sheet.description: Choose two: Insight, Investigation, or Perception. Spend 1 moxie to gain advantage on an Investigation, Insight, or Perception check.

description.p: At 6th level, you can use a bonus action and expend 2 moxie points to hone in on the idiosyncrasies and bad habits of an enemy you can see within 30 feet. For 1 minute or until you use this feature again, you have advantage on weapon attacks against that creature and add your proficiency bonus to your AC against attacks made by that creature.

sheet.description: Choose an enemy you can see within 30 ft. For 1 minute, you have advantage on weapon attacks against it and add your proficiency bonus to your AC against attacks made by it.

description.p: Starting at 11th level, when you take a long rest in a settlement, you can choose to become familiar with that settlement. While in your familiar settlement, you cannot be surprised, add your proficiency bonus to initiative, have darkvision 120 feet, double your proficiency bonus for proficient Insight, Investigation, or Perception checks, cannot be lost by any means, and can travel between any two points in the settlement twice as fast when not in combat.

sheet.description: After a long rest in a settlement, you can make it your familiar settlement. There, you cannot be surprised, add proficiency to initiative, have darkvision 120 ft., double proficiency for proficient Insight, Investigation, and Perception checks, cannot be lost, and travel twice as fast outside combat.

description.p: Starting at 17th level, you can use a bonus action and spend 1 moxie point to open your senses to your surroundings for 1 minute. During this time, you have advantage on saving throws against being blinded or deafened and have truesight out to 30 feet.

sheet.description: For 1 minute, you have advantage on saves against being blinded or deafened and have truesight out to 30 ft.

description.p: When you choose this fight club at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with Animal Handling if you don’t already have it. If you do, you gain proficiency in your choice of Perception or Survival.

sheet.description: You gain proficiency in Animal Handling. If you already have it, choose Perception or Survival instead.

description.p: Also at 3rd level, you gain a hound that accompanies you and fights alongside you. Your hound uses the wolf stat block. Add your proficiency bonus to your hound’s AC, saving throws, attack rolls, and damage rolls. For each pugilist level you gain after 3rd, your hound gains an additional d8 Hit Die and increases its hit points accordingly.

You can use a bonus action on each of your turns to verbally command your hound to take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action that turn. It acts on its own if you are incapacitated or absent. If your hound dies, you can obtain a new one by spending 8 hours bonding with a non-hostile canine animal.

sheet.description: You gain a hound using the wolf stat block. Add your proficiency bonus to its AC, saves, attack rolls, and damage rolls. It gains one extra d8 Hit Die for each pugilist level after 3rd. Command it as a bonus action to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help.

description.p: At 3rd level, when you use certain moxie abilities, your hound gains a benefit as well. Brace Up gives your hound the same temporary hit points. The Old One-Two can let your hound make one or both attacks instead of you. Stick and Move can let your hound take the Dash action.

sheet.description: Brace Up: your hound gains the same temporary hit points. The Old One-Two: your hound can make one or both attacks instead of you. Stick and Move: your hound can take the Dash action.

description.p: At 6th level, your hound’s attacks count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks and damage.

sheet.description: Your hound’s attacks count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to non-magical attacks and damage.

description.p: Also at 6th level, when you use the Attack action on your turn, if your hound can see you, it can use its reaction to make a melee attack.

sheet.description: When you use the Attack action, if your hound can see you, it can use its reaction to make a melee attack.

description.p: At 11th level, when a creature deals damage to your hound with an attack, you can use your reaction to make an opportunity attack against that creature if you are within range.

sheet.description: When a creature damages your hound with an attack, you can use your reaction to make an opportunity attack against it if within range.

description.p: Beginning at 17th level, you use the dire wolf statistics instead of the wolf statistics for your hound, except that its size remains Medium. These statistics are modified by Brawler’s Best Friend.

sheet.description: Your hound uses dire wolf statistics instead of wolf statistics, except its size remains Medium. Apply Brawler’s Best Friend as normal.

description.p: Starting when you choose this fight club at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the Intimidation skill if you do not have it already.

sheet.description: You gain proficiency in Intimidation.

description.p: Also at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to provoke a creature within 60 feet who can see or hear you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, it takes your Fisticuffs die + your Charisma modifier in psychic damage and has disadvantage on attack rolls that do not include you as a target before the start of your next turn.
For your Piss & Vinegar features that require a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

sheet.description: A creature within 60 ft. that can see or hear you makes a WIS save against DC {{pugilist:piss vinegar:dc}}. On a failure, it takes 1d{{pugilist:fisticuffs:dice}} + CHA psychic damage and has disadvantage on attacks that do not include you before your next turn.

description.p: Starting at 6th level, you have three dirty tricks: Heelstomper, Low Blow, and Pocket Sand. You can use each dirty trick once, and regain their use when you finish a short or long rest.
Heelstomper. When you deal damage with an unarmed attack, the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you gain 1 moxie point up to your maximum, and its speed is halved for 1 minute.
Low Blow. When you deal damage with an unarmed attack, the target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, you gain 1 moxie point up to your maximum, and it is knocked prone.

Pocket Sand. As a bonus action, a creature within 5 feet must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, you gain 1 moxie point up to your maximum, and it is blinded until the end of its next turn.

sheet.description: You know Heelstomper, Low Blow, and Pocket Sand. Each can be used once per short or long rest. Saving throw DC: {{pugilist:piss vinegar:dc}}.

description.p: At 11th level, when you make a Charisma (Intimidation) check, you can use your reaction and spend 1 moxie to give yourself advantage. When a creature makes a saving throw against one of your Piss & Vinegar features, you can use your reaction and spend 1 moxie to give that roll disadvantage.

sheet.description: Spend 1 moxie as a reaction to gain advantage on a Charisma (Intimidation) check, or to impose disadvantage on a saving throw against one of your Piss & Vinegar features.

description.p: Starting at 17th level, when you use Salty Salute, you can choose to target a number of creatures within 60 feet who can see or hear you up to your pugilist level instead of a single creature. You gain 1 moxie point, up to your maximum, the first time each creature targeted this way hits you with an attack before the start of your next turn. You can use this feature again after you finish a long rest.

sheet.description: When you use Salty Salute, target up to {{level:pugilist}} creatures within 60 ft. You gain 1 moxie point, up to your maximum, the first time each target hits you before your next turn.

description.p: Starting when you choose this fight club at 3rd level, you gain additional moxie features: Compression Lock, Quick Pin, and To the Mat.
Compression Lock. When a creature succeeds on an attempt to break a grapple with you, you can use your reaction and spend 1 moxie point to force it to roll again and use the second result.
Quick Pin. When a hostile creature’s movement provokes an opportunity attack from you, you can use your reaction and spend 1 moxie point to make a grapple attack instead.
To the Mat. You can use a bonus action and spend 1 moxie point to make a grapple attack against a creature within range. If successful, the creature is also knocked prone.

sheet.description: You gain Compression Lock, Quick Pin, and To the Mat as additional moxie features.

description.p: At 6th level, when you have an enemy creature grappled, you gain half cover against all attacks made against you by creatures you are not grappling. When a weapon attack made by a creature you are not grappling misses you, you may use your reaction and spend 1 moxie point to have that creature make the same attack with a new roll against an enemy creature you are grappling.

sheet.description: While grappling an enemy, you have half cover against attacks from creatures you are not grappling. When such a creature misses you with a weapon attack, spend 1 moxie as a reaction to redirect the same attack against a creature you are grappling.

description.p: At 11th level, you count as one size larger for the purposes of grappling. In addition, you can move your full speed when dragging or carrying a grappled creature your size or smaller.

sheet.description: You count as one size larger for grappling. You can move your full speed when dragging or carrying a grappled creature your size or smaller.

description.p: At 17th level, while you have a creature grappled, you gain advantage on all attacks against it. Additionally, when you make an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon attack against a creature you have grappled, you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

sheet.description: While you have a creature grappled, you have advantage on attacks against it. Your unarmed strikes and pugilist weapon attacks against a grappled creature score a critical hit on 19 or 20.

description.p: Starting when you choose this fight club at 3rd level, you can use your reaction and spend 2 moxie points to reduce the damage of a melee weapon attack made against you by 1d10 + your Strength modifier + your pugilist level. If you reduce the damage to 0, you can make an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon attack against a creature within range as part of the same reaction.

sheet.description: Reduce melee weapon attack damage by 1d10+{{pugilist:cross counter bonus}}. If this reduces the damage to 0, make an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon attack against a creature within range.

description.p: At 6th level, when you use your bonus action to use The Old One-Two and hit the same creature with both attacks, you can spend 1 moxie to make an additional unarmed strike against that creature as part of the same bonus action. If you hit, the creature is knocked prone in addition to taking damage.

sheet.description: When The Old One-Two hits the same creature with both attacks, spend 1 moxie to make one additional unarmed strike against it as part of the same bonus action. On a hit, the target is knocked prone.

element.name: Float Like a Butterfly, Sting Like a Bee

description.p: At 11th level, when you reduce damage from an attack to 0 and successfully hit an enemy creature using Cross Counter, you regain 1 moxie point up to your maximum.

sheet.description: When Cross Counter reduces damage to 0 and you hit with its counterattack, regain 1 moxie point up to your maximum.

description.p: At 17th level, when you hit with an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon, you can spend 1 or more moxie points to try to knock out the opponent instead of dealing damage. Roll 3d12 + 2d12 for every moxie point spent after the first and add your pugilist level. If the total is equal to or greater than the creature’s remaining hit points, it is unconscious for 10 minutes.

sheet.description: When you hit with an unarmed strike or pugilist weapon, spend moxie to knock out instead of dealing damage. Roll 3d12 + 2d12 per moxie spent after the first + {{level:pugilist}}. If the total is at least the target’s remaining hp, it is unconscious for 10 minutes.
